newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to hold Kremlin meetings on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to hold Kremlin meetings on Thursday.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, observing a light work schedule as he recovers from pneumonia, will return to the Kremlin on Thursday to meet the head of the upper house of parliament, his press office said.
"President Yeltsin will definitely come to the Kremlin to meet Federation Council Chairman Yegor Stroyev," a spokesman said.
Yeltsin, 66, fell ill with pneumonia exactly a month ago, and now spends most of his time recovering in an official residence outside Moscow. In November, he had quintuple heart bypass surgery.
Against the advice of his doctors, he has visited the Kremlin a handful of times since leaving the hospital however, most recently on Tuesday to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
The Kremlin did not say what Yeltsin would be discussing with Stroyev, a former communist who has largely been loyal to Yeltsin since assuming the Federation Council's top position.
But recently Stroyev has said that the Russian constitution -- which gives the president overwhelming powers -- should be changed to give the parliament more influence
